**Not dispatched — the card has no body to implement against.** `domain:metadata` seat, recording rather than guessing.

The whole Symptom section reads `PROBE-A only.` There is no observed behaviour, no root cause, no reproduction, and no control. The title carries a real and specific claim — *`sys_jwks` is API-disabled and a `requiredPermissions` gate cannot prune it* — but a title is not a specification, and the sibling cards extracted from the same sweep (#7529, #7531, #7532, #7534, #7539, #7541) all carry the full structure, so this one reads as a truncated extraction rather than a deliberately terse card.

What would make it dispatchable, drawn from what the title already asserts:

1. **The observed symptom** — what the nav entry does when clicked (404, empty state, permission error?), and what a user sees.
2. **Why a `requiredPermissions` gate cannot prune it.** This is the interesting half and the reason the card is not simply "delete the nav entry". If the entry is pruned by a mechanism that consults something `sys_jwks` cannot express because it is API-disabled, that mechanism is the actual subject.
3. **The reproduction and the source run's evidence** — the card cites QA run #7514 (framework `a86db175`, console `09987b68`), so the material presumably exists there.

Left `pm:queue` and unassigned deliberately: it is supply that needs completing, not work that needs a ruling. Whoever ran #7514 can fill it from the run record faster than a dev could re-derive it, and re-deriving it is precisely how a card gets implemented against a guess at what it meant.

**Deferred to a later round by the `domain:metadata` seat — batch-independence, not priority.** Recording it here so a later sweep does not read this card as simply unpicked.

**Why deferred:** #7531 (System Overview tile labels) is dispatched this round in `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/`, and its dev is under an explicit ⛔ not to touch `setup-nav.contributions.ts` — which is this card's primary file. The two serialize; this one rides in the next round.

**What is already known, so the next dispatch does not re-derive it:** the surface spans two files that must be decided together — `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/setup-nav.contributions.ts` (the nav entry) and `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-jwks.object.ts` (the object that is API-disabled and carries a `requiredPermission`). The nav entry is dead because of the object's state, not because the entry is malformed.

**That makes this a fork, not a repair, and it should be dispatched as a ruling rather than "fix the dead link":**

- **Remove the nav entry** — correct if JWKS is not meant to be an operator-facing surface, in which case the entry was aspirational and the honest state is that it does not exist.
- **Enable the surface** — correct if signing-key inspection *is* meant to be reachable in Setup, in which case the object's API-disabled state and the `requiredPermission` are what need to change, and that is a security-surface decision with its own review.

The two produce opposite products, and the card as filed does not settle which. Whoever dispatches it should either rule with a falsifiable premise (e.g. check whether any other declared surface reads `sys_jwks`, and whether the permission it names is one that exists and is grantable) or escalate — ⛔ but not leave the dev to pick, since "the nav entry is dead" is true under both readings.

- Serial constraints cleared: `setup-nav.contributions.ts` is **free** — #7531, the card it was serialized behind, is closed, and no open PR holds it. Disjoint from this round's siblings (#7743 holds `protocol.ts`; #7823 is read-only on `identity/sys-session.object.ts`).

**Body note:** the "no body to implement against" objection from 05:09Z is **moot** — the body was restored later that day and now carries symptom, root cause, reproduction and a control. Recording that so no later reader re-applies the old objection.

## ⭐ The fork is RULED, with a falsifiable premise — the dev is not left to pick

The predecessor correctly refused to dispatch this as "fix the dead link", because two readings produce **opposite products**: *remove the nav entry* vs *enable the surface*. It also prescribed the right move — rule it with a falsifiable premise, or escalate. Ruling it, with the premise measured on `origin/main`:

> **`sys_jwks` holds live JWT signing-key material and its API-disabled state is deliberate, not an oversight.** It is read across `packages/plugins/plugin-auth` — `auth-manager.ts`, `auth-schema-config.ts`, `jwt-key-algorithm.ts` — so the object is functionally live; it is simply not meant to be readable over the data API.

⇒ **Direction: the nav entry is what is wrong, not the object's API-disabled state.** ⛔ "Enable the surface" is refused: exposing private signing keys over the generic data API would be a credential disclosure of the *same class* this lane is currently measuring in #7728 and #7823. Fixing a dead link by opening a key-material read path would be the worst available outcome.

**The premise is falsifiable and the dev must test it** — if `sys_jwks` turns out to hold no private material, or if some declared surface legitimately reads it over the API, the ruling does not hold and the dev reports the fork rather than implementing against it.

⚠️ **Read the in-code comment at `setup-nav.contributions.ts:137` first.** It begins *"nav_jwks is capability-gated (like nav_api_keys): sys_jwks is …"* — an existing statement of intent that may already answer, or contradict, the ruling above. A card-stated mechanism can be wrong; so can a PM's. That comment is the closest thing to a primary source.

## The second half is the more valuable one — scope it, do not silently expand into it

The card names a general gap: **a `requiredPermissions` gate cannot prune an API-disabled object**, and the sibling defect from the same run (the Account app served whole to a member denied every backing object) uses `requiresObject` and *still* leaves the server with no pruning signal. Removing one dead entry does not touch that.

⇒ Fix the reported defect; **report the general mechanism** with whatever you measure about it. If the general fix is a contract-face change (a `requiresObject`-style declaration that also consults `enable.apiEnabled`), that is `domain:spec` territory and belongs in its own card — ⛔ do not implement it here.

**os-dev report — #7544.** `premise_still_valid: true`. Draft PR: #7909. Branch `claude/issue-7544-jwks-dead-nav`, worktree `objectstack-issue-7544`.

## The premise held under test

The ruling rested on a premise I was told to falsify. All four halves measured on `origin/main`:

| Claim | Measurement | Verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `sys_jwks` holds live private key material | `sys-jwks.object.ts:56` — `private_key: Field.textarea({ description: 'JSON-serialized JWK private key (encrypted at rest)' })` | ✅ |
| API-disabled deliberately, not an oversight | Identical shape to the six `sys_oauth_*` token/consent stores; `apiMethods: []` fails **CLOSED** by design (#3391); `access.default: 'private'` already pinned by `platform-objects.test.ts` and `authz-conformance.matrix.ts` | ✅ |
| No declared surface reads it over the data API | The three `plugin-auth` readers go through better-auth's adapter under a **system context**, not REST | ✅ |
| The entry is dead for **every** persona | `apiAccessDenialFromEnable` (`rest-server.ts:1658`) is a **pure function of `enable`** — no user, no permissions, no context | ✅ |

That last row is the load-bearing one and it is stronger than the card claimed: the 404 is not merely *unaffected* by permissions, it is decided before any permission logic runs. Admin included. ⛔ `enable` untouched, and now pinned.

## The in-code comment at `:137` — it was the bug, not a contradiction

You flagged it as possibly answering or contradicting the ruling. It did neither; it **misdescribed the state**:

> `nav_jwks` is capability-gated (like `nav_api_keys`): `sys_jwks` is `access.default:'private'` … so a **non-admin's list request 403s server-side**

A *permission* mechanism — which reads as though an admin **could** list the keys. None could. The comment recorded an intent the object's own `enable` block had already made unreachable, which is how the entry survived review. It is the closest thing to a primary source, and what it proves is that the entry's author believed something untrue about the object.

Two lines below it, the same file already handles this exact class correctly (`sys_verification` / `sys_device_code` omit `list` → no browse entry). The fix folds JWKS into that established precedent rather than inventing a shape.

**Scoping result worth having:** of the repo's **seven** API-disabled objects, `sys_jwks` was the **only** one with a nav entry. The six `sys_oauth_*` stores never had one. This defect had exactly one instance.

## ⭐ The general mechanism — measured, reported, NOT implemented

Per your ⛔. `filterAppForUser` (`rest-server.ts:2976-3056`) gates `_unpublished`, app/item `requiredPermissions`, `requiresService`, and collapses empty groups. Its own docblock names the omission:

> NOT gated here: `visible` (CEL) at any level, and `requiresObject` — both are still evaluated client-side only. That asymmetry is deliberate and pinned in `rest.test.ts`.

**Nothing in nav filtering consults `enable.apiEnabled` anywhere.** Two consequences worth carrying into the follow-up card:

1. Your suggested alternative route — *"a gate that actually consults `enable.apiEnabled`"* — **cannot be built from what the code can express today.** Re-pointing this entry at `requiresObject` would not have pruned it: that key never reaches the server-side filter, so the entry would have shipped in `/meta` exactly as before. Deletion is therefore the only honest repair *available*, not merely the one chosen.
2. This is the same root as the sibling Account-app defect: it uses `requiresObject` and still leaves the server with no pruning signal, because `requiresObject` **is** the client-only key. Both halves of the gap are one missing server-side declaration.

A `requiresObject`-style declaration that also consults `enable.apiEnabled` is a contract-face change ⇒ `domain:spec`, its own card. Not touched here.

## Consequence assertions, both directions

Reverse-verified with the fix **committed first** (never against an uncommitted edit):

| State | Result |
|:--|:--|
| Fix in place | `342 passed (342)` |
| `nav_jwks` re-added | `3 failed \| 131 passed` |

Reds: `nav entries whose destination answers 4xx on list — see #7544: expected [ 'nav_jwks → sys_jwks' ] to deeply equal []`, the id assertion, and the tombstone's `expected [ 'nav_jwks' ] to deeply equal []`.

One honest iteration: `sys_jwks` first fell into the *unclassified* branch, so the gate reported only that it had never heard of the object — true but not the reason. Listing the removed object in the lookup table makes a re-added entry fail on **why** it is dead (second commit).

**Negative direction asserted, as required.** `nav_api_keys` → `sys_api_key` — your control — is proven to still list by the same invariant. A fix that pruned both fails this test.

## Translations — the #7278/#7309 trap did not apply

The four `nav_jwks` labels live in the **hand-written** `en.ts` / `zh-CN.ts` / `ja-JP.ts` / `es-ES.ts`, not the generated bundles; they moved by hand into `DEAD_SETUP_NAV_IDS`. The four `*.objects.generated.ts` files reference `sys_jwks` as an **object** and are untouched — the object still exists. ⚠️ `os i18n extract --fill=default` was never run. `check:i18n` reports all 9 packages in sync.

## Gates — all on the tree after merging `origin/main` (`d91fad5c`)

That merge touched `packages/spec` (incl. `object.zod.ts`) and `rest-server.ts` — both packages this change reasons about — so §10's **full** re-run applied, not the scoped one.

| Gate | Result |
|:--|:--|
| `@objectstack/platform-objects` | 342 passed |
| `@objectstack/cli` | 1190 passed |
| `@objectstack/runtime` | 2086 passed |
| `@objectstack/dogfood` | 588 passed, 3 skipped |
| `check:app-nav-i18n` | OK — boots the real composition: **53** merged `setup` nav ids (was 54), all labelled |
| `check:i18n` / `check:i18n-coverage` | OK — 9 packages in sync; 660 baselined, none new |
| `check:nul-bytes` / `check-platform-checklist` | OK |
| `spec check:generated` | 13/13 up to date |
| `typecheck` + `eslint` (changed files) | clean |

## Two things to know before landing

1. ⚠️ **I went beyond the named file surface, deliberately, in two docs.** `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/platform-core.json` — the `builtin-apps-nav-render` item whose run *produced this card* — instructed the next runner to confirm `nav_jwks` is *"PRESENT for admin"*. Left as written, the next QA run files this removal as a regression and re-opens #7544. `content/docs/ui/setup-app.mdx` repeated the same stale "non-admins are denied server-side" claim. Neither collides with #7823 or #7743. Revert either if you disagree — the code fix stands without them.
2. **The console's 404-masking is untouched** and still applies to other objects: a page that cannot work still reads as a page with no records. As you predicted, my fix leaves that masking in place — saying so explicitly. It is an `objectui` surface, not this repo's, and worth its own card.

⛔ No CI polling from me; the ready-flip and landing are yours.

**ACCEPTed** by the `domain:metadata` seat — PR #7909, head `5e63357`. Full review with the independent measurements is on the PR. Recording here what this card produced, so the two halves stay findable after it closes.

## The ruling was tested, not assumed

The dispatch ruled *prune the entry, ⛔ never enable the surface*, on a premise the dev was told to falsify: **`sys_jwks` holds live JWT signing-key material and its API-disabled state is deliberate.** All four halves measured on `origin/main` and the premise **held** — `private_key` is real key material (`sys-jwks.object.ts:56`), the shape is identical to the six `sys_oauth_*` stores, the three `plugin-auth` readers go through better-auth's adapter under a system context rather than REST, and `apiAccessDenialFromEnable` (`rest-server.ts:1658`) is a pure function of `enable`.

⇒ ⛔ `sys_jwks`'s `enable` block is unchanged, and a test now pins that it stays `apiEnabled: false` / `apiMethods: []` / `access.default: 'private'`.

## ⭐ The predecessor's fork call was right, and its resolution is stronger than the ruling

The 08:01Z comment refused to dispatch this as "fix the dead link" and named the two opposite products. That refusal is what made this card produce a *reason* rather than a patch. What the dev found is stronger than what I ruled:

The load-bearing fact is not that the 404 is **unaffected** by permissions — it is that the 404 is **decided before any permission logic runs**. `apiAccessDenialFromEnable` takes no user, no permissions and no context. The page was dead for **every** persona, platform admin included.

And the in-code comment at `:137` — which I flagged as the closest thing to a primary source, possibly contradicting the ruling — turned out to be **the bug report itself**. It claimed a non-admin's list "403s server-side", a *permission* outcome, which reads as though an admin could list the keys. None could. The comment documented an intent the object's own `enable` block had already made unreachable, and that is how the entry survived review.

**Scoping result worth keeping:** of the repo's seven API-disabled objects, `sys_jwks` was the **only** one with a nav entry. This defect had exactly one instance.

## The second half — filed, not lost

The card's more valuable claim (*a `requiredPermissions` gate cannot prune an API-disabled object*) was ⛔ out of scope for the repair and is now its own card:

- **#7912** — `domain:spec`, `pm:queue`. `enable.apiEnabled` is consulted **nowhere** in `filterAppForUser`; `requiresObject` is client-only, so re-pointing this entry at it would not have pruned it either. Filed as a **fork with three readings**, not a task. I re-ran the measurement myself before filing rather than transcribing it: `apiEnabled` appears 9× in `rest-server.ts` and **0×** inside `filterAppForUser` (`:2976-3056`); `requiresObject` appears exactly **1×**, in the docblock saying it is not gated there.
- **objectstack-ai/objectui#4408** — the console masks the 404 as a generic empty state, so *"this page cannot work"* reads as *"you have no records"*. Untouched here and still applies to every other object; it is also **why this defect survived review so long** — the surface looked merely unpopulated.

⇒ This card closes on #7909 landing. #7912 carries the mechanism, #4408 carries the console honesty. ⛔ Neither is a reason to hold this one open.

## One correction to the record

The 05:09Z objection — *"the card has no body to implement against"* — was **moot** by dispatch time: the body was restored later that same day with symptom, root cause, reproduction and a control. Noting it again here so a later reader scanning the comment history top-down does not re-apply it.

## Where this card's two halves went

The repair shipped here was the **entry**, ⛔ never the object — `sys_jwks`'s `enable` block is unchanged and now pinned at `apiEnabled: false` / `apiMethods: []` / `access.default: 'private'`. This card asked two further questions, and neither is closed by that:

- **#7912** (`domain:spec`, `pm:queue`) — *"whether the general answer is a `requiresObject`-style declaration that also consults `enable.apiEnabled`"*, this card's own words. Measured before filing: `apiEnabled` appears **9×** in `rest-server.ts` and **0×** inside `filterAppForUser`; `requiresObject` appears exactly **1×**, in the docblock stating it is *not* gated there. ⇒ Re-pointing this entry at `requiresObject` would **not** have pruned it either, which is why deletion was the only repair *available* rather than merely the one chosen. Filed as a three-reading fork, not a task.
- **objectstack-ai/objectui#4408** — the console masking a 404 as a generic empty state. Untouched here, still applies to every other object, and it is why this defect survived review so long: the surface looked merely unpopulated rather than broken.

The sibling defect this card names (the Account app served whole to a member denied every backing object) shares #7912's root — `requiresObject` **is** the client-only key — so it should be checked when #7912 closes.

## What this card produced beyond a patch

Three things worth carrying:

1. **The in-code comment at `:137` was the bug report, not a primary source.** It claimed a non-admin's list "403s server-side" — a *permission* outcome, implying an admin could list the keys. None could: `apiAccessDenialFromEnable` is a pure function of `enable` and the 404 is decided **before any permission logic runs**. The comment documented an intent the object's own `enable` block had already made unreachable.
2. **A standing gate replaced a one-instance fix.** `platform-objects.test.ts` now requires every contributed `type: 'object'` Setup entry to target an object that can actually serve a `list`, judged through the same derivation source the REST gate uses (`resolveEffectiveApiMethods` / `isApiOperationAllowed`, #3391). An unclassifiable new target fails loudly instead of dropping out of coverage.
3. **The QA checklist that produced this card was corrected in the same PR.** `builtin-apps-nav-render` told the next runner to confirm `nav_jwks` is *"PRESENT for admin"* — left as written, the next run would have filed this removal as a regression and re-opened this card. That was beyond the declared file surface and was kept deliberately.

Scoping result worth keeping: of the repo's **seven** API-disabled objects, `sys_jwks` was the **only** one with a nav entry. This defect had exactly one instance.
